# Gonex

> A modular Go framework for typed HTTP APIs and explicit service boundaries.

Development snapshot: main branch; no published release yet.

## Documentation
- [Build APIs with Gonex](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/): Install Gonex, generate projects and modules with its CLI, and develop typed JSON APIs with validation, OpenAPI and structured logs.
- [Install Gonex and its CLI](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/installation/): Install Gonex as a Go library and project-local development tool, then generate an API application without cloning the framework.
- [Your first API project](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/quick-start/): Create a Gonex project with the CLI, add an HTTP module, run the server and inspect JSON responses, logs and OpenAPI.
- [Build a REST API](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/building-api/): Build create, list and get user endpoints in a CLI-generated Gonex app, using schemas.go validation, explicit services and OpenAPI.
- [Connect a frontend](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/frontend/): Use Gonex as the backend for a Nuxt, Vue, React or Flutter frontend, with clear API URLs and deployment boundaries.
- [Debug mode and development pages](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/debug/): Use DEBUG=true for the Gonex duck welcome page and browser error diagnostics, while keeping JSON API contracts and production responses unchanged.
- [Application architecture](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/architecture/): Structure a Gonex application around plain Go business services, explicit modules and optional HTTP, database and gRPC adapters.
- [Organize your API project](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/project-structure/): Develop inside a CLI-generated Gonex application with clear service, schema, handler and route responsibilities and protected registries.
- [Modules and lifecycle](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/modules/): Register explicit Go modules, share business services, and manage resources through startup and graceful shutdown.
- [CLI reference](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/cli/): Reference Gonex commands for safe project scaffolding, modules, API versions, gRPC generation and database migrations.
- [HTTP and OpenAPI](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/http/): Build typed HTTP endpoints with Gin adapters, request validation and OpenAPI 3.1 contracts in Gonex.
- [HTTP API versions](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/versioning/): Keep version-specific HTTP adapters and contracts separate while sharing business behavior in Gonex.
- [Databases and migrations](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/database/): Use optional GORM adapters with SQLite or PostgreSQL and explicit, checksum-verified SQL migrations.
- [gRPC and contracts](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/grpc/): Configure optional Gonex gRPC servers and clients, versioned Protobuf contracts, deadlines, TLS and mTLS.
- [Microservices](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/microservices/): Develop independent Go services with explicit typed clients, local diagnostics and supervised processes.
- [First microservice call](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/microservices-quickstart/): Install Gonex, wire Orders to Identity explicitly and run local services with a single supervised command.
- [Microservice diagnostics](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/microservices-troubleshooting/): Resolve local ports, TLS, contract generation, unfinished mapping and supervised process failures.
- [Microservice compatibility](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/microservices-compatibility/): Understand catalog ownership, safe client generation, contract versions and independent Go module deployment.
- [Deploy your application](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/deployment/): Build and host a Gonex JSON API as a Go service, with explicit configuration, readiness and frontend hosting.
- [Server output and logging](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/logging/): Configure readable server startup URLs, correlated request logs, log levels and structured production JSON in a Gonex application.
- [Metrics and tracing](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/observability/): Correlate Gonex request logs and unary RPC traces, collect bounded latency histograms and opt in to Prometheus metrics.
- [Operations and readiness](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/operations/): Configure readiness, graceful shutdown, request metrics, resource ownership and trace propagation.
- [Security configuration](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/security/): Review Gonex request limits, authentication boundaries, CORS policy and secure transport configuration.
- [Application API reference](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/api-reference/): Reference Gonex construction, module registration, typed routing, lifecycle and resource APIs.
- [Compatibility and upgrades](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/upgrades/): Pin Gonex versions and review HTTP, Protobuf and generated-code compatibility before upgrading.
- [Release status](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/release/): Understand the current Gonex development snapshot, dependency pinning and support considerations for application developers.
- [Production readiness](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/production-readiness/): Review Gonex hardening, the standalone PostgreSQL API sample, verification evidence and the remaining production release gates.
- [Contribute to Gonex](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/contribute/): Set up the Gonex framework repository, understand its internals and contribute tested changes to the framework itself.
- [Framework development setup](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/contribute/development-setup/): Fork and clone Gonex, install its Go toolchain, run the source example and test local framework changes from another app.
- [Framework internals](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/contribute/architecture/): Understand Gonex internals: application registration, transport contracts, adapters, package dependencies and generator ownership.
- [Framework testing and verification](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/contribute/testing/): Run Gonex formatting, unit, contract, integration, race and benchmark checks without confusing framework tests with application tests.
- [Prepare a contribution](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/contribute/pull-requests/): Prepare focused Gonex framework pull requests with reproductions, relevant tests, compatible contracts and clear verification notes.
- [Maintaining releases](https://amkargar.github.io/GoNex-website/docs/main/contribute/releases/): Review the Gonex maintainer release checklist, compatibility gates, contracts modules and verification requirements.

## Source
- https://github.com/amkargar/gonex
